# Kinds of subject and their properties

A subject is a reference to something in the simulation, of a known kind; an expression reads its properties: `self.loc`, `here.block.material` (05 §5). A property marked *safe for belief* may be read of anything in a mind context; any other, only of the character's own subject (05 §7.3). One marked *settable* may be assigned with `set`.

| Kind | What it refers to | Properties |
|------|-------------------|-----------:|
| [`ability`](#ability) | An ability an entity holds (08 §3.2), reached as `self.ability('id')`; `ability` in what an ability works out about itself. | 9 |
| [`app`](#app) | Things outside the simulation: saves, profiles, mods, scenarios, preferences and the grid (12 §10.4). | 18 |
| [`app_entry`](#app-entry) | One entry of a list `app` offers: a save, a profile, a mod or a scenario. | 4 |
| [`area`](#area) | A named volume with tags, variables and optionally a clock of its own (02 §8.3). | 14 |
| [`attrs`](#attrs) | The attributes of one entity, reached as `entity.attr` (06 §4.1). | 1 |
| [`element`](#element) | The floor, block or fixture of a cell (16 §3.5), reached as `here.floor`, `here.block` and `here.fixture`. | 18 |
| [`entity`](#entity) | Any entity: a creature, an item, a device (06). | 149 |
| [`functions`](#functions) | What one entity's body can do, reached as `entity.fn` (06 §6.3). | 1 |
| [`global`](#global) | The whole simulation: where global variables live (05 §6). | 3 |
| [`loc`](#loc) | A cell of a grid (02 §3.2). | 31 |
| [`part`](#part) | A part of a body (06 §6). | 23 |
| [`pools`](#pools) | The pools of one entity, reached as `entity.pool` (06 §4.2). | 4 |
| [`realm`](#realm) | One contiguous space with its own rules (02 §4). | 6 |
| [`site`](#site) | A named place with identity, spanning one or more tracts (02 §8.4). | 8 |
| [`tracks`](#tracks) | The tracks of one entity, reached as `entity.track` (06 §4.3). | 2 |
| [`tract`](#tract) | A tract of a realm, loaded or not: what the engine knows of it is its record (02 §9.1). | 10 |
| [`window`](#window) | A reaction window (03 §7.1): an opportunity with a deadline that those who notice it may answer. | 0 |
| [`wound`](#wound) | A wound on a part of a body (06 §7.3). | 11 |

<a id="ability"></a>
## `ability`

An ability an entity holds (08 §3.2), reached as `self.ability('id')`; `ability` in what an ability works out about itself.

- `ability.bound(name: string) -> any`: What its binding of a name holds (08 §7.3), if it is still there: the summoned entity, the area, the one a bound trait or rule is on, or the conjured cells as a list of `loc`; null otherwise.
  Changed by `binding_created`, `binding_ended`.
  - `name` (string): Which.
- `ability.cooldown(action: id<action>) -> real`: Seconds of its owner's own time before the grant of an action can be used again: 0 when it is ready. Moves with time, so it cannot be kept current.
  - `action` (id<action>): Which.
- `ability.def -> id<ability>?`: Its definition.
- `ability.id -> string?`: Its definition's qualified id.
- `ability.mode_on(mode: string) -> bool`: Whether a mode of it, by id, is on (08 §5.4).
  Changed by `mode_started`, `mode_ended`.
  - `mode` (string): Which.
- `ability.owner -> entity?` · same owner: The entity that holds it; null once it is not held.
  Changed by `mind_transferred`, `ability_revoked`.
- `ability.rank -> int`: Its rank: its track's level, or the rank set directly (08 §4.1).
  Changed by `rank_changed`.
- `ability.state -> string?`: `active`, `dormant` (its `while` does not hold; 08 §6.1) or `suppressed` (active, and suppressed from outside; 08 §6.2); null once it is not held.
  Changed by `ability_dormant`, `ability_active`, `ability_suppressed`, `ability_restored`.
- `ability.tags -> list<string>?`: Its definition's tags.

<a id="app"></a>
## `app`

Things outside the simulation: saves, profiles, mods, scenarios, preferences and the grid (12 §10.4). Bound as `app` in every screen.

- `app.can_load -> bool` · safe for belief: Whether the scenario's saving policy allows loading now.
- `app.can_save -> bool` · safe for belief: Whether the scenario's saving policy allows saving now (13 §9.2).
- `app.controls(context?: string) -> list<map<string>>` · safe for belief: Every control the loaded mods define, in order of what it is called, bound or not (12 §9.2): one map for each, with `id`, its qualified id; `label`, its `name`, or else its bare id; `doc`, what it does, or empty; `keys`, every key the keymap in force gives it in the context, as a keymap writes them, joined by commas, or empty; and `shown`, the same keys as a person reads them (`Shift+J`, `Tab`, `F1`, `Esc`).
  - `context` (string, optional): A context of the keymap whose keys are listed: left out, `play`.
- `app.creation -> any` · safe for belief: The character being made (06 §10.3); null when none is.
- `app.defines(type: string) -> bool` · safe for belief: Whether the loaded mods define anything of a definition type: so that a screen offers a setting only for a system that has something to work on (decision D-867). False for a type no loaded definition has, and for one the engine does not know.
  - `type` (string): A definition type, by the name data writes it with: `cutscene`, `recipe`.
- `app.keys(context: string) -> list<map<string>>` · safe for belief: What the keymap in force binds in a context: one map for each name a key there is given, in order of what it is called, with `name`; `label`, what the control of that name is called, or else the name; `doc`, what it does, or empty; `keys`, every key given that name, as a keymap writes them, joined by commas; and `shown`, the same keys as a person reads them (`Shift+J`, `Tab`, `F1`, `Esc`) (12 §9.2).
  - `context` (string): A context of the keymap: `play`, `menu`, `targeting`.
- `app.mods -> list<app_entry>` · safe for belief: The mods that were found, each with whether it is enabled.
- `app.pref(id: id<preference>) -> any` · safe for belief: The value of a preference (12 §10.4).
  - `id` (id<preference>): The preference's id.
- `app.profile -> app_entry?` · safe for belief: The profile in use.
- `app.profiles -> list<app_entry>` · safe for belief: The profiles that can be started (04 §3.3).
- `app.saves -> list<app_entry>` · safe for belief: The saved games, newest first as the application lists them.
- `app.scenario -> app_entry?` · safe for belief: The game scenario being played, if one is.
- `app.scenarios -> list<app_entry>` · safe for belief: The game scenarios the loaded mods define (13).
- `app.setup -> any` · safe for belief: The game being set up on the new-game screens (13 §12): the scenario chosen, its places, the options it asks about and how its seed is chosen; null when none is.
- `app.size -> list<int>` · safe for belief: The grid, as `[columns, rows]`.
- `app.talk -> any` · safe for belief: What the character played could say to someone, as the service `talk` last gathered it (15 §11): a map with `to`, the one talked to; `options`, each a map with `id`, `text`, `kind` and `lines` (the message kind and the table of lines it is said with, null where it says nothing) and `says`, whether it says something; and `why`, the reason nothing can be said, or empty. Null when nothing was gathered.
- `app.target -> any` · safe for belief: The creature selected as the target in play (the `camera` effect's `target`), while the party perceives it; null when none is or it is no longer perceived. Read of it only what may be read of anyone the party perceives.
- `app.templates -> list<app_entry>` · safe for belief: The templates a character may be made from, each by its qualified `id` and its `name` (06 §10.3).

<a id="app-entry"></a>
## `app_entry`

One entry of a list `app` offers: a save, a profile, a mod or a scenario.

- `app_entry.description -> string` · safe for belief: A line or two about it.
- `app_entry.id -> string` · safe for belief: What the entry is known by: a save's file name, a qualified id.
- `app_entry.name -> string` · safe for belief: The name shown to the player.
- `app_entry.state -> string` · safe for belief: Its state, in a word: `enabled`, `disabled`, `broken`, `current`.

<a id="area"></a>
## `area`

A named volume with tags, variables and optionally a clock of its own (02 §8.3).

- `area.breached -> bool?`: Whether the area was made by enclosing a space that no longer closes.
  Changed by `area_breached`, `area_closed`.
- `area.clock_rate -> real?` · settable: The rate of the area's own clock relative to the clock above it, or null if it has none (03 §3.4). Setting a rate gives the area a clock or changes its rate; setting null takes the clock away. Whoever is inside is put on the clock that now applies, and `clock_rate_changed` is emitted.
  Changed by `clock_rate_changed`.
- `area.contains(at: any) -> bool?`: Whether the area covers a cell.
  - `at` (any): A cell, or something that is somewhere.
- `area.def -> id<area_kind>?`: The kind that gave the area its defaults and carries its rules, if it has one.
- `area.grid -> int?`: The id of the grid the area is in.
- `area.has_tag(tag: string) -> bool`: Whether it carries a tag.
  - `tag` (string): The tag to look for.
- `area.kind -> string` · safe for belief: The name of the kind of subject this is: `entity`, `loc`, `element`, `area`, `site`, `tract`, `realm` or `global`.
- `area.loc -> loc?`: The cell at the middle of the area.
- `area.local_time -> real?`: The local time of the area's own clock, in seconds, or null if it has none.
- `area.occupants -> list<entity>`: The entities inside the area, each once, in the order their cells come.
  Changed by `area_entered`, `area_exited`.
- `area.priority -> int?`: Which area applies where several overlap: the highest.
- `area.site -> site?`: The site the area belongs to, if any.
- `area.tags -> list<string>?`: The area's tags, with those its kind gave it, in order.
- `area.timer(name: string) -> real?`: The local time, in seconds, that the timer of this name belonging to it has left (05 §10.4); null if it has none of that name. A timer away with its owner keeps what it had left.
  - `name` (string): The timer's name.

<a id="attrs"></a>
## `attrs`

The attributes of one entity, reached as `entity.attr` (06 §4.1).

- `attrs.value(attribute: id<attribute>) -> real`: The value of an attribute chosen by id, modifiers applied. Null for something with no stats.
  Changed by `attr_changed`.
  - `attribute` (id<attribute>): Which attribute.

<a id="element"></a>
## `element`

The floor, block or fixture of a cell (16 §3.5), reached as `here.floor`, `here.block` and `here.fixture`.

- `element.damage -> int?`: Its accumulated damage, in 255ths of what it can take (02 §12).
  Changed by `element_damaged`, `element_changed`.
- `element.def -> any`: Its definition, as an id of `floor`, `block` or `fixture` according to its layer. Null if the cell holds no such element or is not loaded.
  Changed by `element_changed`.
- `element.def_id -> string?`: The qualified id of its definition, as a text.
  Changed by `element_changed`.
- `element.device -> entity?`: The device entity bound to the element, if it has been promoted (02 §5.5). Null for an element that is plain now, whether or not its definition names a device.
  Changed by `device_promoted`, `device_demoted`.
- `element.has_flag(flag: string) -> bool?`: Whether its state has one of the engine's flags (02 §5.4): `opaque`, `passable`, `load_bearing`, `anchor`, `ramp`, `stairs`, `ladder`, `liquid`, `grate`, `rough` or `fragile`. Null for a name that is not a flag.
  Changed by `element_changed`.
  - `flag` (string): The flag's name.
- `element.has_tag(tag: string) -> bool`: Whether it carries a tag.
  - `tag` (string): The tag to look for.
- `element.height -> real?`: How high it stands from the base of its cell, in metres. Zero for a floor.
  Changed by `element_changed`.
- `element.interactions -> list<string>`: The qualified ids of the interactions the element's definition lists (02 §5.5), in order. Those offered by `any` are not listed.
  Changed by `element_changed`.
- `element.kind -> string` · safe for belief: The name of the kind of subject this is: `entity`, `loc`, `element`, `area`, `site`, `tract`, `realm` or `global`.
- `element.latent -> bool`: Whether generation left contents in the element that have not been made yet (06 §9.3): they are made when it becomes a device (opened, searched, something put in it, damaged) or `materialise_contents` is called on it. False for an element whose contents were made, and for one that never had any.
  Changed by `device_promoted`, `contents_materialised`.
- `element.layer -> string` · safe for belief: Which of its cell's elements it is: `floor`, `block` or `fixture`.
- `element.loc -> loc` · safe for belief: The cell it is in.
- `element.material -> id<material>?`: What it is made of.
  Changed by `element_changed`.
- `element.mode -> string?`: The mode of the device the element gives behaviour to (16 §4.2): its device's, or the first of its device definition's `modes` while it has not been promoted. Null for an element that names no device or one with no modes.
  Changed by `device_mode_changed`, `device_promoted`, `device_demoted`.
- `element.state -> int?`: Its state: the index of the named state its definition declares, or the definition's own number (an amount, a facing).
  Changed by `element_changed`.
- `element.state_name -> string?`: The name of its state, where its definition declares named states.
  Changed by `element_changed`.
- `element.store(resource: string) -> real?`: What the store of a resource of the device the element gives behaviour to holds now: its device's, or its definition's `start` while it has not been promoted. Null for a store it does not have.
  - `resource` (string): The resource, as the device's `stores` name it.
- `element.tags -> list<string>?`: The tags of the element's definition, in order.

<a id="entity"></a>
## `entity`

Any entity: a creature, an item, a device (06). A reference to one that has been removed reads as null.

- `entity.abilities -> list<id<ability>>`: The abilities the entity holds, in the order it gained them.
  Changed by `ability_granted`, `ability_revoked`.
- `entity.abilities_with(tag: string) -> list<ability>` · same owner: The instances of the abilities the entity holds that have a tag, in the order it gained them.
  Changed by `ability_granted`, `ability_revoked`.
  - `tag` (string): The tag.
- `entity.ability(ability: id<ability>) -> ability?` · same owner: The instance of an ability the entity holds (08 §3.2), to read its rank, state, parameters and cooldowns; null if it does not hold it.
  Changed by `ability_granted`, `ability_revoked`.
  - `ability` (id<ability>): The ability: its id, or its qualified id as text.
- `entity.ability_modes -> list<map<any>>`: Every mode of every ability the entity holds (08 §5.4): one row for each, with `ability`, `id`, `name` (the ability's), `mode` (the mode's id), `label` (what the mode is called), `rank`, `on`, `available` and `why`. Read of the character itself in a mind context.
- `entity.ability_uses(ability?: any) -> list<map<any>>`: Every use of every ability the entity holds (08 §5.1, `ability::options`), or of the one named, for an abilities screen: one row for each grant, with `value` (the action's id), `ability` (the ability's id), `label`, `id` (the ability's qualified id), `name`, `action_name`, `rank`, `state` (`ready`, `cooling`, `dormant`, `suppressed` or `unavailable`), `cost` (a text: `25 stamina`), `cooldown` (seconds of its own time left), `given` (the names of the parameters the grant supplies), `available` and `why`. Read of the character itself in a mind context.
  - `ability` (any, optional): An ability: its id, or its qualified id as text.
- `entity.actions_with(tag: string, target?: any) -> list<map<any>>`: What the entity could start of the actions that carry a tag, as it believes (12 §10.7): one row for each, those that could start first, then those that strike with something held, then those that take fewer slots, then by qualified id, with `value` (the action's id), `label` and `name` (what a reader calls it), `id` (its qualified id as a text), `available` (whether it could start now) and `why` (the refusal's sentence where it could not, else empty). With `target`, that is given to an action that has a parameter or role named `target`; its `requires` is judged once every parameter without a default is given. Read of the character itself in a mind context.
  - `tag` (string): The tag the actions carry: the `ui` mod asks for `strike`, `shot`, `grip`, `takedown`.
  - `target` (any, optional): Who the actions are aimed at, if anyone.
- `entity.altitude -> real?`: How high the entity stands above the base of its cell, in metres. Null if it is not at a cell itself.
  Changed by `entity_relocated`.
- `entity.attr -> attrs` · same owner: The entity's attributes: follow with a definition's id, as in `self.attr.<id>`.
- `entity.awareness(x: entity) -> real?`: This mind's awareness of `x` now, the highest through any of its senses, 0 to 1 (15 §5.1). Null if it has none.
  Changed by `suspicion_raised`, `detected`, `lost_track`.
  - `x` (entity): Whom or what it is asked about.
- `entity.believed_loc(x: entity) -> loc?`: Where this mind last perceived `x`, or was told it was (15 §7.2). Null if it never has.
  - `x` (entity): Whom or what it is asked about.
- `entity.bound_by -> entity?`: Whose ability the entity is bound to (08 §7.3), as a summoned servant is to its summoner: the owner of the ability whose `summon` made it, while the binding lasts; null otherwise. A character may read its own: whom it serves.
- `entity.can_interact(target: any, interaction: id<interaction>) -> bool`: Whether the entity, as it believes, can do an interaction to a target now: the target offers it, it is in reach and its `if` holds (16 §3.2). What an interaction's action `requires`.
  - `target` (any): An element or an entity.
  - `interaction` (id<interaction>): The interaction.
- `entity.can_make(recipe: any, station: any) -> bool`: Whether the entity, as it believes, could start or resume a recipe now, by hand or at a station: what a work action `requires`.
  - `recipe` (any): The recipe: its id, or its qualified id as a text.
  - `station` (any): The station: an element or a device; null by hand.
- `entity.can_reach(to: loc) -> bool`: Whether a cell is next to the entity and it believes it can step into it.
  - `to` (loc): The cell.
- `entity.can_step(dir: string) -> bool`: Whether the entity believes it can step in a direction from where it stands: a cell is there and one of its ways of moving makes the step. Who else is in the cell is not asked.
  - `dir` (string): The direction: `north` to `north_west`, `up` or `down`.
- `entity.cannot_use(ability: id<ability>, action?: id<action>) -> string?`: Why the entity cannot use an ability now (08 §5.1), as the reason's code (`ability.cooling_down`, `ability.cost_short`, …); null if it can. With an action, that grant; without, the ability's only one. Moves with time and pools, so it cannot be kept current.
  - `ability` (id<ability>): The ability: its id, or its qualified id as text.
  - `action` (id<action>, optional): The action of the grant; left out, the ability's only one.
- `entity.capacity_mass -> real?`: The most what is stowed in a container may weigh, in kilograms. Null for what is not a container and for one with no limit.
- `entity.capacity_volume -> real?`: The most space what is stowed in a container may take up, in cubic metres. Null for what is not a container and for one with no limit.
- `entity.carried -> list<entity>` · same owner: Everything inside the entity at any depth: what it holds, what those hold, and so on, each container before its contents.
  Changed by `item_taken`, `item_dropped`, `item_worn`, `item_removed`, `entity_relocated`.
- `entity.carried_mass -> real?`: The mass of everything inside the entity, to any depth, in kilograms. Null for one with no physical component.
  Changed by `entity_relocated`.
- `entity.clock_rate -> real?`: How fast time passes for the entity against universal time: the rate of the clock it is on, with every clock above it. Null if it is on none.
- `entity.coating -> map<real>` · same owner: What is coated on an item's striking surfaces (16 §9.5 `coat`): the volume of each substance in cubic metres, by qualified id.
- `entity.color -> string?` · settable: The colour an item carries, by name: one its definition fixed or one picked when it was made. Null for none. Setting it changes it; setting null takes it away.
- `entity.condition -> real?`: How whole an item is, from 1 for undamaged to 0 for broken: one less its damage in 255ths. Null for what is not an item.
  Changed by `item_damaged`, `item_repaired`.
- `entity.conferred_tags -> list<string>`: The tags the entity carries only because something it holds in a grasp or wears confers them, in order.
  Changed by `item_taken`, `item_dropped`, `item_worn`, `item_removed`, `entity_relocated`.
- `entity.confidence(x: entity) -> real?`: How sure this mind is of its track of `x`, 0 to 1: halved for every `mind.confidence_halflife` since it last perceived it (15 §7.2). Null if it never has.
  - `x` (entity): Whom or what it is asked about.
- `entity.config -> map<any>`: A device's settings (16 §4.2 `config`), by id: what its user set, else each one's default. Read as `self.config.enabled`. Null for anything that is not a device.
  Changed by `device_configured`.
- `entity.container -> entity?` · settable: What the entity is directly inside, or null. Setting it puts the entity inside another (`entity_relocated`); setting null takes it out, to where its container is.
  Changed by `entity_relocated`.
- `entity.contents -> list<entity>`: What is directly inside the entity, in id order.
  Changed by `entity_relocated`.
- `entity.control -> string` · settable: Who decides for the entity (03 §5.1): `none`, `direct` or `delegated`. Setting it emits `control_changed`.
  Changed by `control_changed`.
- `entity.could_perceive(at: any, kind: string) -> bool?`: Whether a signal of a kind at a place would reach this mind now through one of its senses (15 §6): a cell, or where an entity stands. Null for a place or a kind that names nothing.
  - `at` (any): A cell, or something that is somewhere.
  - `kind` (string): The signal kind's id, qualified or bare.
- `entity.count -> int?`: How many equal members share the entity: more than one for a stack. Null for what is not an item.
  Changed by `item_split`, `item_merged`.
- `entity.def -> any`: The definition the entity was made from, as an id of whatever type that is. Null for an entity made from none.
- `entity.defending -> bool`: Whether a defence of its own is in force now (07 §5.1): one of its actions with a `defence` is in the phase its `during` names.
  Changed by `phase_entered`, `action_finished`, `action_cancelled`, `action_interrupted`, `action_abandoned`.
- `entity.description -> string?`: The entity's own description, if it has been given one.
- `entity.element -> element?`: For a device bound to an element, the element: what it gives behaviour to (16 §4.1). Null for anything else.
- `entity.facing -> real?`: Which way it faces, in degrees clockwise from north (15 §4). Null for something with no senses.
- `entity.fears(x: entity) -> bool`: Whether this character's mind fears `x`: by a stance it took, or, once it has perceived `x`, by a tag `x` presents that its mind's `fear_of` names.
  Changed by `detected`, `perceived`.
  - `x` (entity): Whom it is asked about.
- `entity.feed -> entity?` · same owner: The store an item fires from (07 §11.5): itself if it is a store, else the first store fitted to it. Null for neither.
  Changed by `entity_relocated`.
- `entity.fill -> real`: How much one member of an item holds in all, in cubic metres.
- `entity.fn -> functions` · same owner: What the entity's body can do: follow with a function's id, as in `self.fn.<id>`.
- `entity.free_grasp(channel: id<channel>) -> int`: How many slots of a channel the working parts of the entity's body supply that nothing it grasps occupies. Zero for something with no body.
  Changed by `item_taken`, `item_dropped`, `item_worn`, `item_removed`, `entity_relocated`.
  - `channel` (id<channel>): The channel.
- `entity.goal -> string?`: The qualified id of the goal this character's mind holds (09 §3.3). Null if none.
  Changed by `goal_adopted`, `goal_done`, `goal_failed`.
- `entity.goal_about -> any`: What the goal this character's mind holds is about: an entity, a memory as a map, a cell, or null (09 §3.2).
  Changed by `goal_adopted`.
- `entity.gripped_by -> entity?` · same owner: Who grips it, the first to have taken hold (07 §9.1); null for no one. Readable of oneself in a mind context.
  Changed by `seized`, `grip_broken`.
- `entity.gripping -> entity?` · same owner: The first creature or thing it grips, in the order taken (07 §9.1); null for none. Readable of oneself in a mind context.
  Changed by `seized`, `grip_broken`.
- `entity.has_ability(ability: id<ability>) -> bool`: Whether the entity holds an ability (08 §3.3), from any source, dormant or not.
  Changed by `ability_granted`, `ability_revoked`.
  - `ability` (id<ability>): The ability: its id, or its qualified id as text.
- `entity.has_component(component: string) -> bool`: Whether the entity has a component of a kind (06 §3.1).
  - `component` (string): The component's name: `identity`, `physical`.
- `entity.has_item(def: id<item>) -> bool`: Whether the entity holds, wears or carries an item of a definition, at any depth: a key in a pocket counts.
  - `def` (id<item>): The item definition.
- `entity.has_tag(tag: string) -> bool`: Whether it carries a tag.
  - `tag` (string): The tag to look for.
- `entity.has_trait(trait: id<trait>) -> bool`: Whether the entity has a trait, from any giver, dormant or not (06 §5).
  Changed by `trait_added`, `trait_removed`.
  - `trait` (id<trait>): The trait: its id, or its qualified id as text.
- `entity.height -> real?`: How tall the entity stands, in metres. Null for one with no physical component.
- `entity.held(hold: string) -> list<entity>` · same owner: What the entity holds in one kind of hold, in order of id: `self.held('grasp')`, `self.held('worn')`, a container's `held('stowed')`.
  Changed by `item_taken`, `item_dropped`, `item_worn`, `item_removed`, `entity_relocated`.
  - `hold` (string): The kind of hold: `grasp`, `worn`, `stowed`, `seat`, `inside` or `fixed`.
- `entity.helpless -> bool`: Whether it cannot resist (07 §10): its mind is not awake (unconscious, or dead), or someone grips it with a pin. What a takedown's `requires_at_start` reads, beside whether the victim perceives the attacker. Reads truth.
  Changed by `entity_unconscious`, `entity_woke`, `entity_died`, `entity_revived`, `seized`, `grip_broken`.
- `entity.hold -> string?`: How the entity is held by what it is inside: `grasp`, `worn`, `stowed`, `seat`, `inside` or `fixed`. Null for one that is inside nothing.
  Changed by `item_taken`, `item_dropped`, `item_worn`, `item_removed`, `entity_relocated`.
- `entity.hold_fault(verb: string, what: any, other?: any) -> string?`: Why the entity, as it believes, could not do one of the holding verbs to a thing now, as a sentence for it to read: null if it could (06 §9.2, decision D-865). For an item action's `requires` and `fail_text`; read of the character itself in a mind context. `take`: pick up a thing lying loose within reach, or take one it carries into a hand (what no hand holds goes into something carried that takes it); `grasp`: hold it in a hand; `drop`; `wear`; `remove`, into a hand; `stow`, into something it wears or holds; `put_in`, into `other`, which it carries or perceives within reach; `take_out`, out of a container it carries or perceives within reach, into a hand; `give`, to `other`, someone it perceives within reach with a hand free for it. Doing it to the entity itself is refused; `take` of the entity itself says there is nothing within reach to pick up.
  Changed by `item_taken`, `item_dropped`, `item_worn`, `item_removed`, `entity_relocated`.
  - `verb` (string): `take`, `grasp`, `drop`, `wear`, `remove`, `stow`, `put_in`, `take_out` or `give`.
  - `what` (any): The thing.
  - `other` (any, optional): For `put_in` the container, for `give` whom it is given to.
- `entity.holder -> entity?`: What holds the entity: what it is directly inside. Null for one that is inside nothing.
  Changed by `item_taken`, `item_dropped`, `item_worn`, `item_removed`, `entity_relocated`.
- `entity.holds_substance(substance: id<substance>) -> real`: How much of a substance one member of an item holds, in cubic metres.
  - `substance` (id<substance>): The substance.
- `entity.home -> loc`: Where this character's mind belongs: where it first thought, or what `set_home` said; for one that has not thought, where it is. Null only for one that is nowhere.
- `entity.hostile(x: entity) -> bool`: Whether this character's mind holds `x` hostile (09 §3.4): by a stance it took, or, once it has perceived `x`, by a tag `x` presents that its mind's `hostile_to` names. Relations (15 §9) will take its place.
  Changed by `detected`, `perceived`.
  - `x` (entity): Whom it is asked about.
- `entity.in_group(group: string) -> bool`: Whether it belongs to a group (15 §9.2), named by key or id.
  Changed by `group_joined`, `group_left`.
  - `group` (string): The group's key or id.
- `entity.in_world -> bool`: Whether the entity is in the world: at a cell, or inside something that is.
  Changed by `entity_relocated`.
- `entity.interaction_fault(target: any, interaction: id<interaction>) -> string?`: Why the entity, as it believes, cannot do an interaction to a target now: null if it can. A refusal's sentence, for an action's `fail_text`.
  - `target` (any): An element or an entity.
  - `interaction` (id<interaction>): The interaction.
- `entity.interaction_time(interaction: id<interaction>) -> real?`: How long an interaction takes, in seconds of the doer's own time (16 §3.1 `time`): what its action's phase lasts. Null for what is not an interaction.
  - `interaction` (id<interaction>): The interaction.
- `entity.is_broken -> bool`: Whether the entity is an item whose damage is all 255 parts.
  Changed by `item_damaged`, `item_repaired`.
- `entity.is_device -> bool`: Whether the entity is a device (16 §4.1).
- `entity.is_item -> bool`: Whether the entity is an item.
- `entity.is_latent -> bool`: Whether the entity is a container whose contents have not been made yet (06 §9.3).
  Changed by `contents_materialised`.
- `entity.item -> id<item>?`: The `item` definition the entity was made from. Null for what is not an item, and for an item made from none: a part that came off a body.
- `entity.kind -> string` · safe for belief: The name of the kind of subject this is: `entity`, `loc`, `element`, `area`, `site`, `tract`, `realm` or `global`.
- `entity.know_how -> list<string>`: The qualified ids of what the entity's mind knows, in order of id.
  Changed by `know_how_gained`, `know_how_lost`.
- `entity.know_how_list -> list<map<any>>`: Every piece of know-how there is, as the entity stands to it, for the know-how screen (12 §10.7): one map each, in order of id: `id`, `name`, `group`, `known`, `ready` (known, or all it needs is known), `makes` (the names of the recipes that need it) and `needs` (the names of what it needs).
- `entity.known_sites -> list<map<any>>`: The sites whose anchor the entity's map memory holds (15 §13), on its grid, nearest first: each with `name`, `at` (the anchor) and `where` (`12 m north-east`). Only directly controlled characters keep a map memory. Read of the character itself in a mind context.
- `entity.knows(x: entity) -> bool`: Whether this mind has a track of what it perceives `x` as (15 §7.2). False for what it has never perceived.
  Changed by `detected`, `lost_track`.
  - `x` (entity): Whom or what it is asked about.
- `entity.knows_element(at: any, layer: string) -> bool?`: Whether this mind knows the floor, block or fixture of a cell for what it is (15 §7.3): it is not tagged `hidden`, or the mind has noted it. Null for a cell that cannot be read or a layer that is not `floor`, `block` or `fixture`.
  - `at` (any): A cell, or something that is somewhere.
  - `layer` (string): `floor`, `block` or `fixture`.
- `entity.knows_how(what: id<know_how>) -> bool`: Whether the entity's mind knows something (16 §8.5): what a recipe's `know_how` and any condition may ask.
  Changed by `know_how_gained`, `know_how_lost`.
  - `what` (id<know_how>): The know-how.
- `entity.knows_name(x: entity) -> bool`: Whether this mind knows the name of whom it takes `x` for (05 §4.6): learnt with `learn_name`, or its own.
  - `x` (entity): Whom it is asked about.
- `entity.last_failure -> string?`: The code of the reason this character's last step or goal failed (09 §16). Null if none has.
  Changed by `step_failed`, `goal_failed`.
- `entity.last_seen(x: entity) -> real?`: Seconds of this mind's own time since it last perceived `x` or heard of it (15 §7.2). Null if it never has.
  - `x` (entity): Whom or what it is asked about.
- `entity.last_seen_at(x: entity) -> real?`: The local time of this mind's clock, in seconds, when it last perceived `x` or heard of it (15 §7.2). Null if it never has.
  - `x` (entity): Whom or what it is asked about.
- `entity.loc -> loc?` · settable: The cell the entity is in: its own, or that of whatever it is inside. Null if it is not in the world. Setting it relocates the entity to stand in that cell (`entity_relocated`); setting null takes it out of the world.
  Changed by `entity_relocated`.
- `entity.local_time -> real?`: The local time of the clock the entity is on, in seconds. Null if it is on none.
- `entity.loose_near -> list<map<any>>`: The things the entity perceives lying loose within reach (in its cell, or one of the eight round it on its storey), its own cell first, then the nearest: what it could pick up. Each a map of `value` (the thing), `label` (what the entity calls it, with its article) and `where` (`here`, `north`, `north-east`, ...), as a list picker takes them (decision D-865). Read of the character itself in a mind context.
  Changed by `item_taken`, `item_dropped`, `item_worn`, `item_removed`, `entity_relocated`.
- `entity.make_fault(recipe: any, station: any) -> string?`: Why the entity, as it believes, could not start a recipe now: null if it could. A refusal's sentence, for a work action's `fail_text`.
  - `recipe` (any): The recipe: its id, or its qualified id as a text.
  - `station` (any): The station: an element or a device; null by hand.
- `entity.making -> map<any>?`: The recipe under way that the entity keeps (16 §8.2): a station's, or work by hand on a worker. A map: `recipe` (its qualified id), `name`, `progress` (the share done now, 0 to 1), `rate`, `worker` (or null) and `why` (why it does not advance, else empty). Null when there is none.
  Changed by `recipe_started`, `recipe_stalled`, `recipe_completed`.
- `entity.mass -> real?`: The mass of the entity and everything inside it, in kilograms.
  Changed by `entity_relocated`.
- `entity.material -> id<material>?`: What an item is made of. Null for what is not an item.
- `entity.memory_confidence(event: string) -> real?`: How sure this mind is of its latest memory of an event type, 0 to 1 (15 §7.1): 1 for what it perceived, less for what it was told (15 §11). Null if it has none.
  Changed by `memory_added`, `memory_forgotten`.
  - `event` (string): The event type.
- `entity.memory_source(event: string) -> string?`: Who told this mind its latest memory of an event type, as the persona it took them for, as text (15 §11). Null if it has none, or perceived it, or did not make out who told it.
  Changed by `memory_added`, `memory_forgotten`.
  - `event` (string): The event type.
- `entity.mind_def -> string?`: The qualified id of the `mind` definition this character thinks by. Null for one that thinks by none.
- `entity.mixture -> map<real>` · same owner: What one member of an item holds (16 §9.5): the volume of each substance in cubic metres, by qualified id. Empty for one that holds nothing.
- `entity.mode -> string?`: The mode a device is in (16 §4.2), by name: one of its definition's `modes`. Null for anything that is not a device, or a device whose definition has no modes.
  Changed by `device_mode_changed`.
- `entity.name -> string?`: The entity's own name, if it has been given one. Null for one that goes by its definition's.
- `entity.next_round -> entity?` · same owner: The round an item's feed gives up next (07 §11.5). Null for an empty one.
  Changed by `item_taken`, `item_dropped`, `entity_relocated`, `entity_removed`.
- `entity.objectives -> list<map<any>>`: The game's objectives and missions as the character knows them, for its journal (14 §13): one row for each, with `kind`, `id`, `text`, `state`, `mission`, `depth`, `marker` and `where`. Read of the character itself in a mind context; a marker follows what the character last perceived of its target.
  Changed by `objective_changed`, `mission_started`, `mission_done`, `mission_failed`, `mission_expired`.
- `entity.occupant_kind -> string`: What the world is told the entity is, for queries: `creature`, `item`, `device` or `other`.
- `entity.offers_near -> list<map<any>>`: What the entity, as it believes, could do within a step: every interaction offered by the elements of its cell and the cells round it on its storey, by what stands there and by what it holds (16 §3.5.1), for a menu. Each is a map: `target` (the element or the entity), `interaction` (its id), `id` (its qualified id as a text), `name` (what a menu calls it), `default` (whether it is the target's default), `available` (whether it can be done now), `why` (the refusal's sentence where it cannot, else empty) and `where` (`here`, `held`, a compass direction such as `north-east`, `up` or `down`).
- `entity.outermost -> entity?`: The entity that is in the world on its behalf: itself, or the container that everything it is nested in is inside.
  Changed by `entity_relocated`.
- `entity.own_mass -> real?` · settable: The mass of the entity alone, in kilograms. Null for one with no physical component. Setting it brings every container round the entity and the world's record of each up to date.
- `entity.own_time -> real?`: How much local time has passed for the entity, on whatever clocks it has been on while it was in the world, in seconds.
- `entity.part(name: string) -> part?` · same owner: A part of the entity's body by name, one that is gone included. Null if the body has no part of that name.
  - `name` (string): The part's name in the body: its `id` in the plan.
- `entity.parts -> list<part>` · same owner: Every part of the entity's body that is there, in the order they were made. Empty for something with no body.
  Changed by `part_severed`, `part_destroyed`.
- `entity.path_cost(to: loc) -> real?`: What the way from where the entity stands to a cell costs, as it believes the way to be: metres of travel at its best speed (09 §6.4). Null if it believes there is none. A search each time it is read.
  - `to` (loc): The cell.
- `entity.path_left -> int?`: How many steps of the path the entity is following are left. Null if it is following none.
- `entity.path_next -> string?`: The direction of the next step of the path the entity is following. Null if it is following none, or is not next to the path's next cell.
- `entity.path_stale -> bool`: Whether the path the entity is following must be planned again before its next step: a step of it was refused, or the entity is not where the path left it.
- `entity.perceives(x: entity) -> bool`: Whether this mind has `x` detected now (15 §6): its awareness reached 1 through some sense and has not fallen to 0.
  Changed by `detected`, `lost_track`.
  - `x` (entity): Whom or what it is asked about.
- `entity.persona -> string`: Its true persona, as text (`7v1/0`) (15 §8.1).
- `entity.persona_of(x: entity) -> string?`: The persona this mind takes `x` for, as text (15 §8.2): what `x` presents, unless this mind has seen through it. Null for something that is not an entity.
  - `x` (entity): Whom it is asked about.
- `entity.pool -> pools` · same owner: The entity's pools: follow with a definition's id, as in `self.pool.<id>`.
- `entity.posture -> id<posture>?`: The posture the entity is in (06 §11.1). Null in none.
  Changed by `posture_changed`.
- `entity.presenting -> string`: The persona it presents now, as text: its true one, one it made, or someone else's it copied (15 §8.1).
- `entity.reach -> real?`: How far the body can reach to strike, in metres: the greatest length, from the trunk out, among its working parts that have a striking surface. Null for something with no body.
  Changed by `part_disabled`, `part_restored`, `part_severed`, `part_destroyed`.
- `entity.recipe_options -> list<map<any>>`: What the entity, as it believes, could make here (16 §8; 12 §10.7 Make): every recipe done by hand, and every recipe of each station within a step, in order of recipe. Each is a map: `recipe` (its id), `id` (its qualified id), `name`, `station` (the element or device, null by hand), `where` (`hand`, `here` or a compass direction), `available`, `resumes` (it goes on with work under way there), `why` (the refusal's sentence, else empty), `work` (seconds at a rate of 1), `inputs` (a list of maps: `what`, `need`, `have`, `text`), `takes` and `gives` (texts).
- `entity.rel(kind: string, x: any) -> real?`: What this mind holds of a kind of relation toward `x` (15 §9.1): an entity, as the persona it takes it for, or a group by key or id. Its own relation, else its groups' (15 §9.2), else the kind's default. Null for a kind or an `x` that names nothing.
  Changed by `relation_changed`, `group_joined`, `group_left`.
  - `kind` (string): The relation kind's id, qualified or bare.
  - `x` (any): An entity, or a group's key or id.
- `entity.remembers(at: any) -> bool`: Whether this character's map memory holds a cell (15 §13): only directly controlled characters keep one.
  - `at` (any): A cell, or something that is somewhere.
- `entity.remembers_actor(x: entity, event: string) -> bool`: Whether this mind remembers whom it takes `x` for as the actor of an event of a type (15 §7.1): `''` for any type. What a witness blames, whoever truly did it (scene S15).
  Changed by `memory_added`, `memory_forgotten`.
  - `x` (entity): Whom it is asked about.
  - `event` (string): The event type, or `''` for any.
- `entity.role_in(group: string) -> string?`: Its role in a group (15 §9.2), or null if it has none or is not a member.
  Changed by `group_joined`, `group_left`, `role_changed`.
  - `group` (string): The group's key or id.
- `entity.room -> real?`: The room left in one member of an item for substances, in cubic metres. Null for what holds none.
- `entity.rounds -> int`: How many rounds an item can fire before it is empty (07 §11.5): the members of the rounds in its feed. Zero for one with none.
  Changed by `item_taken`, `item_dropped`, `item_merged`, `item_split`, `entity_relocated`, `entity_removed`.
- `entity.scale -> real?`: The body's overall size factor. Null for something with no body.
- `entity.seen_how(x: entity) -> string?`: How this mind last knew of `x`: the qualified id of the kind of signal it perceived it by, or `told`, `inferred` or `carried` (15 §7.1). Null if it never has.
  - `x` (entity): Whom or what it is asked about.
- `entity.shot(name: string) -> real?`: One of the numbers a shot through an item takes (07 §11.5): `spread`, `efficiency`, `noise`, `flash` or `energy`, the product of the item's own `shot` number and those of everything fitted to it that states it. Null where none states it.
  Changed by `item_taken`, `item_dropped`, `entity_relocated`.
  - `name` (string): `spread`, `efficiency`, `noise`, `flash` or `energy`.
- `entity.site -> site?`: The site of the cell the entity is in, its own or that of whatever it is inside (02 §8.4): null outside every site and out of the world. Kept current for an objective by `entity_relocated`.
  Changed by `entity_relocated`.
- `entity.speed -> real?`: How fast the entity moves now by the fastest of its ways of moving that works, its posture included, in metres for each second of its own time. Null if it cannot move.
- `entity.stance(x: entity) -> string?`: How this character's mind stands toward `x`: `hostile`, `feared`, or null for neither.
  - `x` (entity): Whom it is asked about.
- `entity.stance_to(x: any) -> string`: How this mind stands toward `x` (09 §3.4): `opposes` if it holds a kind flagged `opposes` above its default by more than any flagged `sides_with`, `sides_with` the other way round, else `neutral`. Read through its groups as `rel` is.
  Changed by `relation_changed`, `group_joined`, `group_left`.
  - `x` (any): An entity, or a group's key or id.
- `entity.standing_orders -> int`: How many orders it keeps that still stand (15 §10).
  Changed by `order_given`, `order_cancelled`.
- `entity.step -> string?`: The kind of the step this character's mind is at: `go`, `do`, `choose`, `wait`, `look`, `say`, `set`, `settle`, `stance`, `keep_near` or `keep_from` (09 §4). Null if it holds no goal or has chosen no method.
- `entity.step_fault(dir: string) -> string?`: Why the entity believes it cannot step in a direction, as a sentence; null if it believes it can.
  - `dir` (string): The direction: `north` to `north_west`, `up` or `down`.
- `entity.step_time(dir: string) -> real?`: How long the entity expects a step in a direction to take, in seconds of its own time: the length of the step it believes lies there, with what its way of moving makes of rough ground and climbing, over that way's speed now. What a phase's `time` waits before the step is taken and checked against the world as it then is. Null if it believes it cannot make the step, or `dir` is not a direction.
  - `dir` (string): The direction: `north` to `north_west`, `up` or `down`.
- `entity.store(resource: string) -> real?`: What a device's store of a resource holds now (16 §5.2), in the resource's unit, less what a recipe under way has drawn from it. Null for a store it does not have.
  - `resource` (string): The resource, as the device's `stores` name it.
- `entity.store_of(tag: string) -> entity?` · same owner: The first store the entity has that takes things carrying a tag (07 §11.5): itself, then what it holds in any way but enclosed, in order of id, and what is fitted to those. A quiver worn, a magazine fitted to a rifle held. Null for none.
  Changed by `item_taken`, `item_dropped`, `item_worn`, `item_removed`, `entity_relocated`.
  - `tag` (string): A tag the store takes.
- `entity.stowed_volume -> real?`: The space what is directly inside the entity takes up, in cubic metres. Null for an entity that is gone.
  Changed by `item_taken`, `item_dropped`, `item_worn`, `item_removed`, `entity_relocated`.
- `entity.tags -> list<string>?`: The entity's tags, in order.
- `entity.time_rate -> real?` · settable: The rate of the entity's personal clock relative to the clock of where it is, or null if it has none (03 §3.5). Setting a rate gives it a personal clock or changes its rate; setting null takes the clock away. Either emits `clock_rate_changed`.
  Changed by `clock_rate_changed`.
- `entity.timer(name: string) -> real?`: The local time, in seconds, that the timer of this name belonging to it has left (05 §10.4); null if it has none of that name. A timer away with its owner keeps what it had left.
  - `name` (string): The timer's name.
- `entity.told_of(event: string) -> bool`: Whether this mind's latest memory of an event type was told rather than perceived (15 §11).
  Changed by `memory_added`, `memory_forgotten`.
  - `event` (string): The event type.
- `entity.track -> tracks` · same owner: The entity's tracks: follow with a definition's id, as in `self.track.<id>`.
- `entity.trait_active(trait: id<trait>) -> bool`: Whether the entity has a trait that is not dormant from some giver: one whose `while` holds, so that it confers what it lists.
  - `trait` (id<trait>): The trait: its id, or its qualified id as text.
- `entity.trait_left(trait: id<trait>) -> real?`: How long until a trait ends by itself, in seconds of the entity's own time: the longest over its givers. Null if the entity does not have it, or has it from a giver for as long as that giver lasts.
  - `trait` (id<trait>): The trait: its id, or its qualified id as text.
- `entity.trait_stacks(trait: id<trait>) -> int`: How many stacks of a trait the entity has, over every giver: 0 for one it does not have, 1 for each giver of one that does not stack.
  Changed by `trait_added`, `trait_removed`.
  - `trait` (id<trait>): The trait: its id, or its qualified id as text.
- `entity.traits -> list<id<trait>>`: The traits the entity has, each once, in the order it first gained them.
  Changed by `trait_added`, `trait_removed`.
- `entity.volume -> real?`: The space the entity takes up, in cubic metres. Null for one with no physical component.
- `entity.weight(name: string) -> real`: This character's mind's weight of a name (09 §3.1), with what the mind's `adjust` entries whose conditions hold add; 0 if it has none.
  - `name` (string): The weight's name, as the mind writes it.
- `entity.wielding(tag: string) -> entity?` · same owner: The first thing the entity holds in a grasp, in order of id, that carries a tag; any thing, for an empty tag. Null for none.
  Changed by `item_taken`, `item_dropped`, `entity_relocated`.
  - `tag` (string): The tag; empty for any.
- `entity.wielding_surface(surface: string) -> entity?` · same owner: The first thing it holds in a grasp, in order of id, whose definition has a striking surface of this id (07 §3.2): the knife or the club whose `flat` a parry puts in a blow's way. Null for none. Readable of oneself in a mind context, so that a reaction's `requires` can say it cannot be done with nothing to do it with.
  Changed by `item_taken`, `item_dropped`, `entity_relocated`.
  - `surface` (string): The id of the surface: `flat`, `edge`, `face`.
- `entity.worn_on(part: string) -> list<entity>` · same owner: What the entity wears over one part of its body, outermost first. A broken item is not listed: it is no longer a layer.
  Changed by `item_taken`, `item_dropped`, `item_worn`, `item_removed`, `entity_relocated`.
  - `part` (string): The part's name in the body.
- `entity.wounds -> list<wound>` · same owner: Every wound on the entity's body, oldest id first. Empty for something with no body.
  Changed by `wound_inflicted`, `wound_healed`.

<a id="functions"></a>
## `functions`

What one entity's body can do, reached as `entity.fn` (06 §6.3).

- `functions.value(function: id<body_function>) -> real`: The capacity of a function chosen by id. Null for something with no body.
  Changed by `function_changed`.
  - `function` (id<body_function>): Which function.

<a id="global"></a>
## `global`

The whole simulation: where global variables live (05 §6).

- `global.kind -> string` · safe for belief: The name of the kind of subject this is: `entity`, `loc`, `element`, `area`, `site`, `tract`, `realm` or `global`.
- `global.now -> real` · safe for belief: Universal time, in seconds since the simulation began.
- `global.timer(name: string) -> real?`: The local time, in seconds, that the timer of this name belonging to it has left (05 §10.4); null if it has none of that name. A timer away with its owner keeps what it had left.
  - `name` (string): The timer's name.

<a id="loc"></a>
## `loc`

A cell of a grid (02 §3.2). It need not be loaded: what cannot be read of it is null.

- `loc.areas -> list<area>`: The areas that cover the cell, in id order.
  Changed by `area_entered`, `area_exited`.
- `loc.atmosphere -> id<atmosphere>?`: The atmosphere at the cell. Null is vacuum.
- `loc.block -> element?`: The cell's block, or null if it has none or is not loaded.
  Changed by `element_changed`.
- `loc.clock_rate -> real?`: How fast time passes at the cell against universal time: the rate of the clock things there run on, with every clock above it.
  Changed by `clock_rate_changed`.
- `loc.field(kind: string) -> int?`: The level of a field in the cell, 0 to 255 (02 §16): 0 where there is none of it, null for a cell that is not loaded or a field no definition names. `cells` queries test it in `where`: `it.field('core:fire') > 0`.
  Changed by `field_appeared`, `field_vanished`.
  - `kind` (string): The field's qualified id.
- `loc.fixture -> element?`: The cell's fixture, or null if it has none or is not loaded.
  Changed by `element_changed`.
- `loc.floor -> element?`: The cell's floor, or null if it has none or is not loaded.
  Changed by `element_changed`.
- `loc.gravity -> real?`: Ambient gravity at the cell in m/s², downward: its stratum's, as the areas that cover it change it.
- `loc.grid -> int` · safe for belief: The id of the grid the cell is in.
- `loc.has_flag(flag: string) -> bool?`: Whether the cell has one of the flags derived from its elements (02 §6.2): `walk_blocked`, `opaque`, `has_floor`, `solid_top` or `fragile`. Null for a cell that is not loaded or a name that is not a flag.
  Changed by `element_changed`.
  - `flag` (string): The flag's name.
- `loc.has_tag(tag: string) -> bool`: Whether it carries a tag.
  - `tag` (string): The tag to look for.
- `loc.in_area(kind: id<area_kind>) -> bool`: Whether an area of a kind covers the cell.
  - `kind` (id<area_kind>): The kind of area.
- `loc.in_area_tagged(tag: string) -> bool`: Whether an area that carries a tag covers the cell.
  - `tag` (string): The tag to look for.
- `loc.is_loaded -> bool`: Whether the cell is inside its grid and its tract is loaded.
  Changed by `tract_loaded`, `tract_unloading`.
- `loc.is_open -> bool?`: Whether the cell is open: it holds nothing and cannot be stood in.
  Changed by `element_changed`.
- `loc.kind -> string` · safe for belief: The name of the kind of subject this is: `entity`, `loc`, `element`, `area`, `site`, `tract`, `realm` or `global`.
- `loc.light -> real?`: How bright the cell is now (15 §3.3): what the sky and the fixed sources give it. Null for a cell that is not loaded.
- `loc.local_time -> real?`: The local time of the clock things at the cell run on, in seconds.
- `loc.obstacle_height -> real?`: The height in metres of the tallest block or fixture in the cell that is in the way.
  Changed by `element_changed`.
- `loc.occupants -> list<entity>`: The entities that have a cell of their footprint here, in id order.
  Changed by `entity_relocated`.
- `loc.realm -> realm?` · safe for belief: The realm the cell's grid belongs to.
- `loc.site -> site?`: The site the cell's tract belongs to, or null.
- `loc.standable -> bool?`: Whether the cell can be stood in: it has a floor, or the cell below has a block with a solid top (02 §5.2). Null for a cell that is not loaded.
  Changed by `element_changed`.
- `loc.tags -> list<string>?`: The tags of the definitions of the cell's floor, block and fixture, in order. Null for a cell that is not loaded.
- `loc.time_of_day -> real?` · safe for belief: The time of day at the cell, in seconds since midnight, by the sky its stratum names. Null where there is no sky. Safe for belief: anyone may know the hour, as a screen's clock shows it (decision D-872).
- `loc.timer(name: string) -> real?`: The local time, in seconds, that the timer of this name belonging to it has left (05 §10.4); null if it has none of that name. A timer away with its owner keeps what it had left.
  - `name` (string): The timer's name.
- `loc.tract -> tract?` · safe for belief: The tract the cell is in. Null for a cell outside its realm, or of a grid that is not a realm's base grid.
- `loc.under_open_sky -> bool?`: Whether nothing stands between the cell and the sky above it.
  Changed by `element_changed`.
- `loc.x -> int` · safe for belief: The cell's coordinate east.
- `loc.y -> int` · safe for belief: The cell's coordinate south.
- `loc.z -> int` · safe for belief: The cell's storey.

<a id="part"></a>
## `part`

A part of a body (06 §6).

- `part.attached -> list<part>` · same owner: The parts that are there and are attached on it.
- `part.condition -> real`: Its condition, from 0 to 1: 1 less each layer's weight times its damage. 0 for a part that is gone.
- `part.def -> id<body_part>`: What kind of part it is.
- `part.exposed -> bool`: Whether it is there and on the outside: it sits inside no other part.
  Changed by `part_severed`, `part_destroyed`.
- `part.girth -> real`: How far across it is, in metres.
- `part.has_tag(tag: string) -> bool`: Whether the part's definition carries a tag.
  - `tag` (string): The tag.
- `part.inside -> list<part>` · same owner: The parts that are there and sit inside it.
- `part.label -> string`: What a reader calls the part: the `name` its body's plan gives it, or else its side and its definition's name (`left arm`).
- `part.layer_damage(layer: int) -> real?`: How damaged a layer is, from 0 to 1. Null if the part has no such layer.
  - `layer` (int): Which layer, from 0 for the outermost.
- `part.layer_material(layer: int) -> id<material>?`: What a layer is made of. Null if the part has no such layer.
  - `layer` (int): Which layer, from 0 for the outermost.
- `part.layer_thickness(layer: int) -> real?`: How thick a layer is, in metres. Null if the part has no such layer.
  - `layer` (int): Which layer, from 0 for the outermost.
- `part.layers -> int`: How many layers it is built of. 0 for a part that is gone.
- `part.length -> real`: How long it is, in metres.
- `part.mass -> real`: Its mass, in kilograms. 0 for a part that is gone.
- `part.name -> string`: The part's name in its body.
- `part.owner -> entity` · same owner: Whose body it is a part of.
- `part.parent -> part?` · same owner: The part it is joined to. Null for the root.
- `part.reach -> real`: How far it can reach from the trunk, in metres: its own length and that of every part between it and the root.
- `part.side -> string?`: Its side label, if the plan gave it one.
- `part.size -> real`: The area it presents, in square metres: its length times its girth.
- `part.state -> string`: `whole`, `disabled`, `severed` or `destroyed`.
  Changed by `part_disabled`, `part_restored`, `part_severed`, `part_destroyed`.
- `part.working -> bool`: Whether it is there and not disabled.
  Changed by `part_disabled`, `part_restored`, `part_severed`, `part_destroyed`.
- `part.wounds -> list<wound>` · same owner: The wounds on it.
  Changed by `wound_inflicted`, `wound_healed`.

<a id="pools"></a>
## `pools`

The pools of one entity, reached as `entity.pool` (06 §4.2).

- `pools.frac(pool: id<pool>) -> real`: A pool's level as a fraction of the most it holds, from 0 to 1; 0 for a pool that holds nothing. Null for something that does not have the pool.
  - `pool` (id<pool>): Which pool.
- `pools.level(pool: id<pool>) -> real`: A pool's level now. Null for something that does not have the pool.
  - `pool` (id<pool>): Which pool.
- `pools.max(pool: id<pool>) -> real`: The most a pool holds. Null for something that does not have the pool.
  - `pool` (id<pool>): Which pool.
- `pools.rate(pool: id<pool>) -> real`: What a pool gains in a second of its owner's time: its regeneration and every rate applied, summed. Negative while it drains. Null for something that does not have the pool.
  - `pool` (id<pool>): Which pool.

<a id="realm"></a>
## `realm`

One contiguous space with its own rules (02 §4).

- `realm.clock_rate -> real?` · settable: The rate of the realm's clock against universal time (03 §3.4). Setting it changes the rate and emits `clock_rate_changed`; a realm always has a clock, so null is refused.
  Changed by `clock_rate_changed`.
- `realm.def -> id<realm>?`: The realm's definition.
- `realm.grid -> int?`: The id of the realm's base grid.
- `realm.kind -> string` · safe for belief: The name of the kind of subject this is: `entity`, `loc`, `element`, `area`, `site`, `tract`, `realm` or `global`.
- `realm.local_time -> real?`: The local time of the realm's clock, in seconds.
- `realm.timer(name: string) -> real?`: The local time, in seconds, that the timer of this name belonging to it has left (05 §10.4); null if it has none of that name. A timer away with its owner keeps what it had left.
  - `name` (string): The timer's name.

<a id="site"></a>
## `site`

A named place with identity, spanning one or more tracts (02 §8.4).

- `site.has_tag(tag: string) -> bool`: Whether it carries a tag.
  - `tag` (string): The tag to look for.
- `site.kind -> string` · safe for belief: The name of the kind of subject this is: `entity`, `loc`, `element`, `area`, `site`, `tract`, `realm` or `global`.
- `site.loc -> loc?`: The cell that stands for the place: its door, its heart.
- `site.name -> string?` · settable: The site's name, as shown. It can be set.
- `site.realm -> realm?`: The realm the site is in.
- `site.tags -> list<string>?`: The site's tags, in order.
- `site.timer(name: string) -> real?`: The local time, in seconds, that the timer of this name belonging to it has left (05 §10.4); null if it has none of that name. A timer away with its owner keeps what it had left.
  - `name` (string): The timer's name.
- `site.tracts -> list<tract>`: The tracts the site spans, in order.

<a id="tracks"></a>
## `tracks`

The tracks of one entity, reached as `entity.track` (06 §4.3).

- `tracks.amount(track: id<track>) -> real`: What a track has accumulated, 0 for one never advanced. Null for something with no stats.
  - `track` (id<track>): Which track.
- `tracks.level(track: id<track>) -> int`: A track's level, 0 for one never advanced. Null for something with no stats.
  Changed by `track_advanced`.
  - `track` (id<track>): Which track.

<a id="tract"></a>
## `tract`

A tract of a realm, loaded or not: what the engine knows of it is its record (02 §9.1).

- `tract.activity -> string?`: How active the tract is, as of the last safe point (02 §10.1): `hot`, `warm`, or null for one the tickets do not keep.
- `tract.devastation -> int?`: How devastated the tract is, 0 to 255 (02 §17.2). Null for a tract with no record.
- `tract.kind -> string` · safe for belief: The name of the kind of subject this is: `entity`, `loc`, `element`, `area`, `site`, `tract`, `realm` or `global`.
- `tract.loaded -> bool`: Whether the tract is loaded.
  Changed by `tract_loaded`, `tract_unloading`.
- `tract.loc -> loc?` · safe for belief: The tract's cell with the lowest horizontal coordinates, at storey 0, in its realm's base grid.
- `tract.realm -> realm` · safe for belief: The realm the tract is in.
- `tract.site -> site?`: The site the tract belongs to, or null.
- `tract.surveyed -> bool`: Whether the tract's region has been surveyed, so that the tract has a record.
- `tract.x -> int` · safe for belief: The tract's coordinate east, in tracts.
- `tract.y -> int` · safe for belief: The tract's coordinate south, in tracts.

<a id="window"></a>
## `window`

A reaction window (03 §7.1): an opportunity with a deadline that those who notice it may answer. A handle that outlives its window reads as closed.

No properties.

<a id="wound"></a>
## `wound`

A wound on a part of a body (06 §7.3).

- `wound.age -> real`: How long ago it was made, in seconds of its owner's time.
- `wound.area -> real`: Its area, in square metres.
- `wound.depth -> int`: How many of the part's layers it goes through, from the outside.
- `wound.energy -> real`: The joules the part absorbed in making it.
- `wound.kind -> id<damage_type>`: The kind of damage that made it.
- `wound.kind_name -> string`: The kind of damage that made it in plain words, for a reader: its damage type's bare id with spaces for underscores (`cut`).
- `wound.owner -> entity` · same owner: Whose wound it is.
- `wound.part -> part` · same owner: The part it is on.
- `wound.rate -> real`: What it drains from pools each second, every pool summed. 0 once it is closed.
  Changed by `wound_closed`, `wound_reopened`.
- `wound.state -> string`: `open` or `closed`.
  Changed by `wound_closed`, `wound_reopened`.
- `wound.stump -> bool`: Whether it is where a part came off.
